extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Jerusalem Post and general readers interested in journalism ethics, Israel–Gaza coverage, and media awards
extracted.subtask_description: An opinion column critiquing Pulitzer Prize decisions and journalistic practices around Gaza coverage, focusing on photography, sourcing, captions, and the ethical standards awards should enforce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid publishing propaganda
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images that are staged, framed, or presented in ways that push an adversary's narrative (e.g., masked pallbearers carrying a coffin adorned with politically charged signage) should be treated as propaganda rather than neutral reportage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vetting contributors' affiliations and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Hamas cultivated ties with a group of Gazans who contributed photographs, and often words, to the world’s top media outlets. Hamas trained young journalists and gave them prizes for loyalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and award committees should investigate whether freelance contributors were selected, trained, or rewarded by interested parties; ties to parties to a conflict can bias coverage and should influence publication and award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and neutrality of captions/labels
rubrics_metrics.description: In his caption, Alghorra labeled them 'prisoners,' the same word he used to describe Shiri, Ariel, and Kfir Bibas, as well as Oded Lifschitz.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word choice in captions (e.g., 'prisoner' vs. 'convicted murderer' vs. 'hostage') materially affects reader understanding; captions must accurately reflect status and avoid euphemisms or misleading equivalences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for ethical/physical boundaries in newsgathering
rubrics_metrics.description: We called into question the physical and ethical boundaries crossed to obtain [photos].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crossing ethical or legal boundaries to obtain material (for example, infiltrating combat zones or entering areas in ways that endanger subjects or journalists) can invalidate the moral standing of images and should be a factor in publication and prize consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider recipients' prior statements when awarding prizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Miller neglected to mention that Alghorra had justified the Oct. 7 attacks ... the Pulitzer Prize Committee announced ... Alghorra would receive this year’s prize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarding bodies should vet laureates' public statements and behavior (including justifications of violence or denialist rhetoric) because such history can contradict the ethical principles prizes claim to honor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not honor voices that deny victims or justify violence
rubrics_metrics.description: You claim to honor journalism that upholds truth, democracy, and human dignity, and yet you have chosen to elevate a voice that denies truth, erases victims, and desecrates the memory of the murdered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prizes and editorial platforms should refrain from elevating writers/photographers whose work or public conduct denies victims, promotes hate, or implicitly/explicitly excuses violent acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify photo provenance and context before awarding or publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: There were small coffins for redheaded children Ariel and Kfir ... and there was a larger coffin for their mother, Shiri, which contained the body of a random Gazan woman and caused massive anguish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers and award committees should verify who/what is actually depicted, the source and chain of custody of images, and whether images have been used or presented in misleading contexts (e.g., misidentified bodies) before conferring honors or wide circulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess social-media conduct and spread of disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Mosab Abu Toha ... spread antisemitic content and fake news on his social media platforms ... In virulent social media posts, Abu Toha disparaged female Israeli hostages, questioned their hostage status, and implicitly justified their abduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A candidate's social-media behavior — including dissemination of hate speech or deliberate misinformation — should be weighed when evaluating suitability for awards and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards should reflect stated values (truth, democracy, human dignity)
rubrics_metrics.description: You claim to honor journalism that upholds truth, democracy, and human dignity ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection criteria for journalism prizes ought to be explicitly aligned with and enforceable against stated values; committees should withdraw or withhold honors that contradict those values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutinize categories and institutional responses for accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee simply eliminated the award for commentary and decided to stop giving it. From this year on, there are prizes for opinion pieces, but the last Pulitzer winner for commentary will be its most shameful and profane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional changes (eliminating categories, renaming awards) should be examined for whether they address underlying selection failures or merely avoid accountability; transparent standards are preferable to cosmetic fixes.
